title: [06/03/2025] Spending on five products by 18-20 year olds
prompt: The chart below shows the spending (in millions) by 18-20 year olds in one country on five different products in 2010 and 2014. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The bar chart compares expenditure by 18-20 year olds on five product categories between 2010 and 2014, with figures given in millions.

frame.name: Overall
paragraphs: Overall, spending patterns showed mixed trends over the four-year period, with smartphones experiencing the largest growth while books recorded a dramatic decline. Food remained the dominant expenditure category throughout both years.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Examining the highest spending areas, food dominated young adults' budgets in 2010 at around 3,700 million, significantly exceeding smartphone spending at 2,000 million. By 2014, food expenditure had risen to 4,300 million, representing a substantial increase of 600 million. Smartphone spending, meanwhile, surged even more dramatically to 2,700 million, marking the largest absolute growth among all categories.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Regarding the remaining categories, clothing, books and toiletries displayed varied patterns. In 2010, clothing accounted for 2,500 million, books for 1,000 million, and toiletries for 1,900 million. However, by 2014, book purchases had plummeted to 500 million, representing the steepest decline. Conversely, clothing expenditure remained completely unchanged at 2,500 million, while toiletries showed modest growth to 2,000 million.
